intelligence.essence: The day is the citizen's world, designed whole. It opens with what matters most: a notification bar first — inbox, messages, loves, comments, actions — across all three worlds, because a day that opens with anything else hides why you came. The greeting lives in the top bar with the date, warm the way the Hub's good morning is warm; the numbers stand as big blocks across the top; and the day's frequency is a real diamond — a spinning jewel of light, never a flat mark, never faster than twelve seconds a turn. The weekday stands as straight words in the day's color, light embedded in the letters, no button and no pill; all seven weekday names fit whole at phone and desktop width, because a cut-off word is an elegance failure. One headliner says the date once. Inside, the day's color fills the whole room — you are inside the day, not beside it — and the design is discerned, not copied: the reference is a lesson, and the question is always what is most intelligent here. The everyday world is seven simple things, each one tap away.
intelligence.human_view: Your day opens with what's calling for you — messages, loves, replies — warmly greeted, with your numbers big and clear and a small jewel turning slowly to carry the day's color. Nothing is cut off, nothing is said twice, and when you step into a day, the whole room takes on its color so you feel where you are.
intelligence.child_view: Imagine your day as a room painted in its own color, with a shiny diamond slowly spinning over the door. The day's name is written big and whole — never squished — and the first thing you see is who wants to talk to you.
intelligence.grandma_view: The calendar used to squeeze the long day-names until they broke. Now every name fits in full, the date is said once and said beautifully, and the day greets you by name in the morning. Stepping into a day feels like stepping into a room made for it.
intelligence.ai_view: Day-design law distilled from SN-3105..SN-3114: (1) the day menu opens with the notification bar (inbox, IMs, likes, comments, loves, shares, actions) spanning Personal + Business + Space. (2) The greeting sits in the top bar with the date, warm as the Hub reference; numbers render as big blocks across the top. (3) The Hz diamond is a real spinning jewel (≤12s/turn), the frequency made visible — never flat. (4) Month view: all seven weekday names fit whole at both widths; the weekday is a royal object (Marcellus, elevated, day-colored). (5) The weekday renders as straight raised words in the day's color with embedded light — no button, no pill; abbreviations solve fit. (6) One headliner carries date + time, said once, judged at full screen. (7) Discern, don't copy: references are lessons; choose the most intelligent display for this surface. (8) The day's color fills the interior — the inside of a day is a room with an atmosphere. (9) The everyday world = seven simple things, each one tap away. (10) Completed means the whole thing — calendar AND Personal, every part — done in the right way, team locked in.
intelligence.what_it_means: The calendar is not a grid with appointments; it is the citizen's world rendered as days. Every ruling in this decade serves that: attention first (notifications), identity always (the greeting), time made beautiful (the jewel, the fitted words), and immersion (the colored room) — a day you enter, not a table you scan.

page.machine: 1) Day opens on notifications across all three worlds. 2) Greeting + date in the top bar; big number blocks. 3) Frequency = spinning jewel object, period ≥12s. 4) Weekday names never truncate at any width. 5) Weekday = raised words, day color, embedded light; no container. 6) Date/time stated exactly once per view. 7) References inform, never template. 8) Day interior = full color fill. 9) The seven everyday things each ≤1 tap. 10) Completion = whole surface, all parts, right way.
page.why_it_matters: The day view is where a citizen will live most of their NayaNET life. These ten dictations, given in one afternoon over live screenshots, are the difference between a calendar that administers a person and a day that welcomes them — and every one of them is checkable at a glance.
page.how_it_connects: Fourth essence of batch 13, covering the Nov 17 afternoon calendar dictations in filing order. It depends on SN-4729's object law (the diamond and the weekday are objects, not drawings) and feeds the surfaces SN-4732's sweep later settles (day view top stays, rest goes).
page.what_is_in_it_for_you: Your day greets you, shows you who needs you, and wraps you in its own color — with every word whole and every number clear. Planning stops feeling like administration and starts feeling like walking into a room that was made for today.
page.the_learning: From now on, we design the day as a place a person enters — attention first, color throughout, nothing truncated, nothing repeated — instead of a grid a person operates.
